bull_bear.body: First-ever dividend recommended (20%); Net debt reduction of INR 156cr in FY26; India debt (~INR 300cr) target repayment in 1-1.5 years via operating cash flows; International debt (~INR 350cr) self-liquidating from local cash flows; Furlenco stake (43%) held for valuation uplift via future IPO.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Raw material volatility (TDI/Polyol prices oscillating INR 180-220/kg); Geopolitical tension in Middle East impacting supply chains; Integration execution risks in international subsidiaries; Competitive intensity in unorganized segment.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident and execution-focused; Emphasis on 'profitable growth' over sheer scale; Transparent on RM volatility but assured of pass-through capability; Strategic patience on Furlenco IPO and international divestment opportunities.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Depreciation policy changed to align with 40-50 year asset life (from aggressive WDV), reducing front-loaded expense skew; U2O value growth (111%) outpacing volume (65%) indicates successful mix-shift to higher ASP models, not just volume push; Furlenco ROCE at 30-35% significantly exceeds parent's ~18%, hidden value driver.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

business.body: Mattress: Vol +13% (Q4), Value +13% (Q4); Foam: Vol +34% (Q4), Value +36% (Q4); U2O: Vol +65%, Value +111% (FY26) driven by higher ASP models; E-commerce: Brand.com +136%, Platforms +39% (FY26); International: Australia Rev INR 422cr (EBITDA 10%), Spain Rev INR 391cr (EBITDA 10.4%).
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Raw material price volatility squeezing smaller unorganized players unable to hedge or pass on costs. | Sheela Foam Ltd | beneficiary | High | Management confirmed market share gains in Q4 as smaller competitors failed to supply during RM spikes; integrated supply chain ensures continuity. |
| Furlenco's path to profitability and scale required capital and operational discipline. | Furlenco (Unlisted) | beneficiary | Med | PAT surged to INR 60cr from INR 3cr; Sheela Foam's 43% stake offers significant optionality upon planned IPO. |
| European margin compression due to energy costs and demand slowdown. | European Competitors | loser | Low | Sheela's Spain/Australia ops improved margins to ~10% via restructuring, suggesting peers without similar efficiency programs may lose share. |
business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Leadership is framed as "Founders with pedigree: ably supported by professionals" — Rahul Gautam (Chairman & MD), Tushaar Gautam (Vice Chairman & Joint MD), Rakesh Chahar (Deputy MD & Whole time Director) and Amit Kumar Gupta (Group CFO).
- The deck reports on two perimeters: a standalone block captioned "Standalone (SFL + KEL)" and a consolidated block; the consolidated perimeter adds Joyce (Australia), Interplasp (Spain) and Staqo, each of which gets its own P&L slide.
- Deck headline slide reads "Leading The Industry, Raising The Bar" and "Strong Growth, Stronger Profitability"; standalone reporting is split into Mattress and Foam, with Foam further split into Technical Foam, Comfort Foam and Furniture Cushioning.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [E-commerce] Q1 FY27 e-commerce is called out as the volume driver, with 19% YoY sales growth on platforms and 69% YoY sales growth on brand.com.
- [Milestone] The deck flags "1ST TIME EVER in Q1" crossing Rs 1000 Cr+ revenue and Rs 100 Cr+ EBITDA (consolidated basis).
- [U2O] A slide titled "Q1 FY27 | Strengthening U2O outreach" carries the counts 24+, 9900+, 230+ and 5500+, but the labels for these four numbers are lost in extraction, so none of them can be attributed to a metric.
- [CSR reporting gap] The CSR initiative slides show the column headings (Key Objective, FY26 Achievements, Q1FY27 Achievements) with the cells rendering only as "In actions", so no CSR outcome figures are stated.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: Core EBITDA margin 11.5% (Q4) vs 7.5% (Q4FY25); Raw materials (TDI/Polyol) up 25-35% YoY but largely passed through; Price hikes implemented across B2C/B2B/Industrial; Inventory turnover (~10-15 days) mitigates lag effects; Depreciation guidance INR 140-145cr for FY27 following policy realignment to match asset useful life (40-50 yrs).
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue Growth: >15% volume growth targeted for FY27; Margin: Core EBITDA margin trajectory >11-12% bracket; Order Inflow: U2O and E-commerce prioritized for penetration; Capex: INR 125-150cr for FY27 (maintenance + debottlenecking + new stores).
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Not applicable for B2C/B2B model; Demand visibility driven by 600 net new showrooms added in FY26 and 8,400 U2O dealers.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Pillow category monetization (previously freebie); Furlenco scaling to INR 500cr (FY27) with potential IPO in 12-15 months; U2O expansion into deeper tier-3/4 towns; Staqo digital arm monetization.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Sheela Foam delivered record FY26 profitability (PAT up 78% YoY) driven by successful Kurlon integration and volume-led operating leverage, validating the shift from growth-at-all-costs to profitable scale. The first-ever dividend declaration and rapid debt reduction signal a mature capital allocation phase, while U2O and e-commerce channels provide structural growth runways despite elevated raw material costs.

open.item: Pursue growth in select adjacent categories, including premium and luxury mattresses and foam-led solutions.
Continue to expand market reach through a deeper physical retail network, including COCO stores, while strengthening e-commerce presence with a sharper focus on the brand.com channel.
Strengthen raw material capabilities to improve supply resilience, reduce exposure to external volatility and support sustainable, profitable growth.
Company is guided on its path to become a net-debt-free entity, having reduced net debt by H156 crore to H543 crore (Net Debt/EBITDA at 1.3x) during FY26.
Strengthen customer engagement, advance innovation and enhance operational excellence across the business in the coming year.
Continue advancing the Sustainability 2030 roadmap covering renewable energy, water stewardship and resource-efficiency initiatives.

B2B segment expected to maintain steady growth, expanding in high-value applications across automotive and packaging, increasing participation in certified segments such as railways, buses and aviation, and strengthening presence in acoustic and other value-added solutions.
Continue import-substitution initiatives aligned with localisation priorities and development of eco-friendly, low-emission and recyclable foam solutions.
Continue to scale presence in the GCC region through e-commerce platforms, retail expansion and local partnerships.

risks.note: Management flags that inflation, interest-rate movements and economic slowdown may impact consumer demand and input costs, given the company's exposure to discretionary consumer spending on mattresses and comfort products.
risks.risk: Macroeconomic sensitivity of demand and input costs

risks.note: Fluctuations in raw material availability and supply chain disruptions can affect production efficiency and product quality; the Company relies on strategic sourcing, bulk procurement and supplier diversification to manage this.
risks.risk: Raw material availability and supply chain disruption

risks.note: Inventory management is flagged as critical, as excess stock could lead to higher carrying costs and potential obsolescence.
The industry continues to witness intense competition from both organised and unorganised players, exerting pressure on pricing and margins.
risks.risk: Intense competition from organised and unorganised players

risks.note: Evolving regulatory requirements and the presence of counterfeit products pose risks to compliance and brand integrity, addressed via robust quality processes, product authentication measures and market surveillance.

Changing consumer preferences towards innovative, sustainable and digitally enabled products, along with a growing shift towards online purchasing, are reshaping demand patterns and require continued digital/omni-channel investment to stay aligned.
risks.risk: Shifting consumer preferences and channel disruption

risks.note: Global uncertainties, including geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and Strait of Hormuz shipping disruptions, and volatility in crude oil prices (a key PU-foam feedstock driver), are flagged as key risks introducing input-cost uncertainty, longer transit times and elevated freight costs.
risks.risk: Geopolitical tensions and crude-oil price volatility

risks.note: Global trade growth is projected to moderate, reflecting evolving tariff structures and increasing protectionist policies, which management flags as a source of uneven growth and cautious business sentiment across regions the Company operates in (India, Australia, Spain, GCC).
